# SnapDisk

> SnapDisk is a free Android app that backs up photos and videos to a USB disk. Plug in a USB disk, tap Backup in the notification, and photos copy oldest-first in the background — no account, no cloud, no ads. Free core (manual backup, 5 GB per run); SnapDisk Pro is a one-time $9.99 purchase for auto-backup on disk connect and unlimited backup size.

## Download

- [Download SnapDisk v0.1.2 (APK, 11 MB)](https://github.com/dzianisv/photo-backup/releases/download/v0.1.2/app-release.apk): free Android app, needs Android 7.0 or later. Not on Google Play yet.
- [All releases](https://github.com/dzianisv/photo-backup/releases): every shipped version with its APK.

## About

- [SnapDisk landing page](https://dzianisv.github.io/photo-backup/): what it does, how it works, pricing, FAQ.
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/dzianisv/photo-backup): Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Material 3.
- [Privacy Policy](https://dzianisv.github.io/photo-backup/privacy.html): collects nothing — no account, no analytics, no ads, no internet permission.

the Agni 2 5G&#x27;s microSD slot is two things — a hybrid slot per smartprix and an expandable 256 GB dedicated slot per Flipkart, no slot at all per mobiledokan and mysmartprice — so check the tray on your unit before buying a card; the Agni 3 5G&#x27;s microSD slot is two things too — no slot at all per smartprix, GSMArena, notebookcheck and techspecs, a dedicated or hybrid slot per phonepik — so the same check applies, and the weight of the sources says no slot; the Blaze X 5G&#x27;s microSD slot is two things — no slot per smartprix and mysmartprice, a microSDXC slot per gsmfind; the Yuva 2&#x27;s second camera is two things — an 8 MP ultrawide per phonepik, a VGA sensor per smartprix; the Yuva 3 Pro&#x27;s second camera is two things — a 0.3 MP auxiliary lens per beebom, an 8 MP ultrawide per phonepik; the Yuva 2 Pro&#x27;s microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 256 GB per 91mobiles, gadgetsnow and smartprix, with bajajfinserv listing the ceiling as not available; VaultDrive needs Android 8 or later per its own site, so every covered Lava phone clears it — and AppBrain lists 12.1 or later, which twelve of the fourteen clear — the Yuva 2 and Yuva 2 Pro run Android 12, below 12.1; no source found names the stock file manager on a Lava phone, so Method 2 uses Files by Google or the built-in file manager, whatever it is called on your unit; no source found states a microSD ceiling for the Blaze 2 5G, the Yuva 3 or the Yuva 3 Pro at all — only that they take microSD — so check the card slot on your unit before buying a card larger than 256 GB for any of those three; FotoSafe needs Android 9 or later with USB host or OTG support, so no covered Gionee phone clears it either; one spec site lists a second F205 Pro and a second S6 entirely — phonepik&#x27;s pages say both were released 15 June 2023 on Android 14 with a 6.67-inch display — against the February 2019 F205 Pro launch on Android 8.1 with a 5.45-inch display and the November 2015 S6 launch on Android 5.1.1 with a 5.5-inch display that every other source lists — so neither 2023 listing is used as a source here; no source found names the stock file manager on a Gionee phone, so Method 2 uses Files by Google or the built-in file manager, whatever it is called on your unit; and the search results for this query are a Dr.Fone guide, two YouTube videos and two generic Android guides — not one of them is a Gionee-specific guide at all. - [Back up Coolpad photos to a USB drive (no computer)](https://dzianisv.github.io/photo-backup/coolpad-photos-to-usb.html): Coolpad is a Chinese telecommunications equipment company headquartered in Shenzhen, Guangdong — its predecessor Yulong Computer Telecommunication Scientific was incorporated on 29 April 1993 in Shenzhen, it started making mobile phones in 2002, Coolpad was originally the smartphone brand of Yulong, and it was later acquired by Jia Yueting and became part of the LeEco Group — and the covered models are the Cool 3 (2019), Note 6 (2018), Note 8 (2018), Mega 5 (2018), Mega 5A (2018), Cool Play 6 (2017), Note 5 Lite (2017), Note 5 (2016), Note 3S (2016), Mega 3 (2016), Mega 2.5D (2016), Cool 1 Dual (2016), Note 3 Plus (2016), Note 3 Lite (2016) and Note 3 (2015) (Cool 3; Note 6; Note 8; Mega 5; Mega 5A; Cool Play 6; Note 5 Lite; Note 5; Note 3S; Mega 3; Mega 2.5D; Cool 1 Dual; Note 3 Plus; Note 3 Lite; Note 3), and Coolpad has no phone-to-USB backup tool of its own: no Coolpad-specific backup advice turned up in any source beyond a computer copy, Google Drive, or Google Photos. Twenty-three honest caveats up front: the one-tap route exists on one phone only — the Cool 3 clears Android 7.0 and lists USB OTG — so only it gets the automated backup; five phones clear Android 7.0 but their OTG is half-stated or disputed — the Note 6, Note 8, Mega 5, Mega 5A and Cool Play 6 — so on those five SnapDisk installs but the one-tap route is unproven until a drive mounts; nine phones run below Android 7.0 and cannot run SnapDisk at all — the Note 5 Lite, Note 5, Note 3S, Mega 3, Mega 2.5D and Cool 1 Dual on 6.0, and the Note 3 Plus, Note 3 Lite and Note 3 on 5.1 — so on those nine there is no SnapDisk route and no rival-app route either, only the computer copy and, on thirteen of the fifteen, the card-reader route; the connector splits the range in two — the Cool 1 Dual and Cool Play 6 take USB Type-C, so a USB-C flash drive plugs straight into those two, while the other thirteen take micro-USB and need a micro-USB OTG adapter — and a USB-C adapter does not fit a micro-USB port, so check your unit&#x27;s port before buying anything; thirteen phones take a microSD card — the Cool Play 6&#x27;s slot is disputed: gadgets360 lists expandable storage Yes, while mobigyaan, techlomedia, pc-tablet and 91mobiles say it takes none — and the Cool 1 Dual takes no card at all — so the card-reader route in Method 4 is proven on thirteen, disputed on the Cool Play 6 and absent on the Cool 1 Dual; the Note 6&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 7.1.1 per gadgets360, 7.1 per gadgetsnow and smartprix — and its processor is two numbers — Snapdragon 435 per gadgets360, telecomtalk and timesnownews, Snapdragon 425 per androidauthority and notebookcheck; the Note 8&#x27;s OTG is disputed — gadgets360 and gadgetsnow leave the line blank, mobilespecs lists micro USB with OTG and mobilegizmo lists USB OTG Support Yes, while a gadgets360 user comment says &quot;This phone is not supporting OTG&quot; — and its microSD slot is two listings — a hybrid slot per gadgets360, a dedicated slot per mobilegizmo — and its chipset is two numbers — MT6750 per the spec page, MT6750T per the launch report; the Mega 5&#x27;s microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 64 GB per gadgetsnow and giznext, up to 128 GB per mobilegizmo — and its OTG is half-stated — gadgets360 leaves the line blank, mobilegizmo lists USB OTG Support Yes; the Mega 5A&#x27;s microSD slot is two listings — a dedicated slot per mobilegizmo, uses the SIM 2 slot per phonesdata — and its OTG is half-stated — gadgets360 leaves the line blank, mobilegizmo lists USB OTG Support Yes; the Cool Play 6&#x27;s OTG is disputed — gadgets360 lists USB OTG No, techlomedia and pc-tablet say it supports USB OTG — and its microSD slot is disputed too — gadgets360 lists expandable storage Yes, mobigyaan, techlomedia, pc-tablet and 91mobiles say it takes none — and its battery is two numbers — 4060 mAh per most sources, 4000 mAh per rechargemytopup, moneycontrol and smartprix; the Cool 3&#x27;s processor is three listings — a 1.3 GHz octa-core Unisoc per gadgets360&#x27;s launch report, a 1.6 GHz octa-core SC9863A per smartprix, and a 1.3 GHz quad-core MediaTek Helio A22 per rechargemytopup — and its rear camera is two numbers — 13 MP + 0.3 MP per smartprix, 8 MP + 0.3 MP per indiatvnews — and its front camera is two numbers — 8 MP per smartprix, 5 MP per rechargemytopup; the Note 5&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 6.0 per gadgets360, 6.0.1 per gadgetguide4u, mobigyaan and gadgetsnow — and its microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 64 GB per gadgets360, up to 128 GB per techulator and phonesdata — and its battery is two states — non-removable per gadgets360, removable per gizmochina — though the disputes change nothing for the backup, since it runs Android 6.0; - [Back up Elephone photos to a USB drive (no computer)](https://dzianisv.github.io/photo-backup/elephone-photos-to-usb.html): Elephone is a Chinese smartphone brand founded in 2006 in Shenzhen — it claims over 1,000 employees and annual sales of over 10 million units — and the covered models are the P3000S (2015), P6000 (2015), P7000 (2015), P8000 (2015), P9000 (2016), P9000 Lite (2016), P20 (2016), P8 (2017), P8 3D (2018), P8 Max (2017), P11 (2018), P11 3D (2019), U (2018), U Pro (2018) and U2 (2019) (P3000S; P6000; P7000; P8000; P9000; P9000 Lite; P20; P8; P8 3D; P8 Max; P11; P11 3D; U; U Pro; U2), and Elephone has no phone-to-USB backup tool of its own: no Elephone-specific backup advice turned up in any source beyond a computer copy, Google Drive, or Google Photos — the closest thing is the devicesfaq backup FAQ, which names the computer copy as the most economical method and the file manager as Files, or Files by Google. Twenty-five honest caveats up front: the one-tap route exists on four phones only — the U Pro, P11, P11 3D and U2 clear Android 7.0 and list USB OTG — so only those four get the automated backup; two phones clear Android 7.0 but their OTG is half-stated — the U and P8 3D — so on those two SnapDisk installs but the one-tap route is unproven until a drive mounts; two more phones clear Android 7.0 but no source states OTG for them at all — the P8 and P8 Max — so on those two SnapDisk installs but the one-tap route is unproven too; seven phones run below Android 7.0 and cannot run SnapDisk at all — the P3000S and P6000 on 4.4, the P7000 on 4.4 or 5.0, the P8000 on 5.0 or 5.1, and the P9000, P9000 Lite and P20 on 6.0 — so on those seven there is no SnapDisk route and no rival-app route either, only the computer copy and, on fourteen of the fifteen, the card-reader route; the connector splits the range in two — the P9000, P9000 Lite, P20, P11, P11 3D, U, U Pro and U2 take USB Type-C, so a USB-C flash drive plugs straight into those eight, while the other seven take micro-USB and need a micro-USB OTG adapter — and a USB-C adapter does not fit a micro-USB port, so check your unit&#x27;s port before buying anything; fourteen phones take a microSD card — and no source found states a card slot for the P20 at all — so the card-reader route in Method 4 is proven on fourteen and unproven on the P20; the P3000S&#x27;s chipset is two numbers — MT6592 per XDA, MT6752 per findpare — and its RAM is two numbers — 2 GB per XDA and findpare, 3 GB per advertentiex; the P6000&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 4.4.4 per androidauthority and gizchina, 5.0 per phonesdata — the 5.0 was a promised over-the-air update, not the shipped version; the P7000&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 4.4 KitKat upgradable to 5.0 per ibtimes, 5.0 out of the box per phonearena; the P8000&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 5.0 per ibtimes, 5.1 per androidheadlines and UL benchmarks — and its battery is two numbers — 4165 mAh per ibtimes and androidheadlines, 4200 mAh per phonearena; the P9000&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 6.0 per most sources, 6.0 and 7.0 per devicesfaq — and its microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 256 GB per gizchina and techadvisor, up to 128 GB per techbloat — and its rear camera is two numbers — a 21 MP camera promised in the pre-launch announcement per gizchina, a 13 MP Sony IMX258 in the shipped phone per gizchina&#x27;s review; the P9000 Lite&#x27;s storage is two numbers — 32 GB in the shipped phone, 16 GB in the pre-launch announcement per gizchina — and its OTG failed in a hands-on test — an XDA reviewer could not read OTG devices on the Lite with USB-C adapters — though the Lite runs Android 6.0 either way and cannot run SnapDisk; the P20&#x27;s Android is 6.0 only as a promise — gizchina&#x27;s announcement piece says Elephone promised Android 6.0 Marshmallow — and no source found states a microSD slot for it at all, so the card-reader route is unproven on it too; the P8&#x27;s RAM is two numbers — 6 GB per most sources, 4 GB per loginby, with phonesdata listing both a 4 GB and a 6 GB model — and no source states OTG for the 2017 P8 at all — the OTG Yes listings on findpare and phonesdata belong to a second, older phone also called Elephone P8, from 2014 on Android 4.1 with a MediaTek MT6592 — so neither listing is used for the 2017 P8 here; the P8 3D&#x27;s own page contradicts itself — phonecorridor&#x27;s key specs say Android 7.0, a 13 MP + 0.3 MP rear camera with a 16 MP front camera, a 4050 mAh battery, a 5.5-inch display and up to 128 GB with a memory card, while the full-spec table on the same page says Android 4.4.2 KitKat, a 13 MP rear camera with a 5 MP front camera, a 2800 mAh battery, a 5.75-inch display and up to 64 GB — the table is copied from the 2014 P8, so the key specs are used here and the table is not; the P8 Max&#x27;s battery is two numbers — 5000 mAh in naijatechguide&#x27;s text, 5060 mAh in its specs table — and no source states OTG for it at all — gizmochina lists only micro USB v2.0 with charging and mass storage, phonesdata lists only USB Yes; the P11&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 8.0 per most sources, 8.1 per unite4buy — and its storage is two numbers — 128 GB per naijatechgist and smartprix, 64 GB per unite4buy — and its microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 256 GB per naijatechgist and philnews, up to 512 GB per smartprix — and its RAM is two numbers — 4 GB per most sources, 3 GB in naijatechgist&#x27;s key-features list; the P11 3D&#x27;s storage is two numbers — 64 GB per phonecorridor, 128 GB per findpare — and its USB port is two states — USB Type-C per phonecorridor, no USB Type-C per findpare — and its rear camera is two numbers — 16 MP + 2 MP per findpare, 13 MP + 2 MP in droidafrica&#x27;s text against 16 MP + 2 MP in its own table; the U&#x27;s Android is two numbers — 7.1 per gizmochina, smartprix and philnews, 8.0 per wemobiles — and its OTG is half-stated — techreviewer says the USB-C socket has OTG support, wemobiles lists OTG support as Not Available — and its microSD ceiling is two numbers — up to 128 GB per gizmochina and smartprix, up to 1 TB per phonearena; the U Pro&#x27;s microSD ceiling is one number with no second source — up to 1 TB per phonearena, while UL benchmarks lists microSD support with no ceiling; the U2&#x27;s chipset is two numbers — Helio P70 per smartprix, Helio P60 per wovow — and its battery is two numbers — 3250 mAh per smartprix and whatmobile, 4000 mAh per wovow — and its rear camera is two numbers — 16 MP + 5 MP + 2 MP per smartprix, 12 MP + 5 MP + 5 MP per wovow — and its storage is two listings — 6 GB and 128 GB per smartprix, 4 GB or 6 GB with 64 GB or 128 GB per whatmobile; VaultDrive needs Android 8 or later per its own site, so four of the fifteen can run it — the P11, P11 3D, U Pro and U2 — and AppBrain lists 12.1 or later, which no covered Elephone phone clears, since the newest covered model runs Android 9; FotoSafe needs Android 9 or later with USB host or OTG support, so two of the fifteen clear it — the P11 3D and U2; the file manager on an Elephone phone is Files, or Files by Google, per devicesfaq — so Method 2 names it directly; and the search results for this query are five iPhone guides — not one of them is an Elephone-specific guide at all.
